1. (Ali Mohammad Magrey,J)
2. 1. These petitions have come to be listed before this Court to be heard alongwith PIL no.01/2012 concerning implementation of the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

However, the learned counsel for the parties submitted at the Bar that the controversy raised in these petitions is not directly related to the issues involved in the PIL, therefore, these petitions may be disposed of separately.
Mr. T.A Lone learned Dy.AG has submitted reply/objections to OWP no. 1277/07.
Same is taken on record.
Copy whereof has been furnished to learned counsel for petitioner.
With consent of the learned counsel for the parties, these petitions are taken up for final disposal.
2. We have heard counsel for the parties and considered the matter.

3. The controversy involved in these petitions revolves around clause 3 of the Jammu and Kashmir Mutton (Licensing and Control) Order, 1973 (for short, 973 Order) issued by the Government of Chinar Sheep And Goat Suppliers Welfare ... vs State Of J&K And Ors on 24 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129687876/
1 Jammu and Kashmir, Ministry of Food and Supplies & Transport Department, vide Notification,
SRO 646 dated 19.12.1973 in exercise of the powers under Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 read with Government of India, Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Food) Notification G. S. R. 316(E) dated 20.06.1973.

sentences.text:
Clause 3 of the 1973 Order read as under:
. Licensing of Dealers, Brokers and Wholesalers:
(1) No person shall carry on the business of Mutton as a Wholesaler, Broker or a Retailer except under and in accordance with a licence issued in this behalf by the Licensing Authority.
(2) A separate licence shall be obtained by a Wholesaler, Broker or Retailer for each place of business. Under SRO 311 dated 13.06.1979

, clause 3 of the 1973 Order was amended by inserting a proviso after sub-clause (1) to the following effect:
Provided that nothing contained in this Clause shall apply to import of Mutton into the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Reading the principal Clause 3 of the 1973 Order and the proviso inserted vide SRO 311 dated 13.06.1979 conjointly
, it becomes axiomatic that no licence is required for purposes of importing Mutton into the State.

It may be mentioned here that in terms of definition Clause 2 of the 1973 Order,
Mutton means a dressed meat of a sheep or goat and includes a live sheep or goat.

It is revealed that some of the clauses of the 1973 Order underwent amendments from time to time but the aforesaid Clause 3, after it was amended by SRO 311 dated 13.06.1979 to the extent indicated above, has remained intact and unchanged.
One such amendment was made vide Notification, SRO 169 dated 16.06.2005 whereby Clauses 4 and 6 of the 1973 Order relating to Issue of Licence and Period of Licence and fee chargeable
were amended.

Under the heading conditions for issuance of wholesale licence certain conditions were added under Sub-clause (3) of Clause 4. Condition no. (1) so incorporated read that the applicant should be bona fide Kothdar having 5 years experience in trade duly certified by Union.

Similarly, condition (7) read that the applicant should be registered with Kothdar Union.
The said amendments came to be challenged by the petitioners herein in writ petition, OWP no.299/2005.

By Court ad interim order dated 16.11.2005 passed in CMP no.853/2005,
accompanying the writ petition, it was ordered that the petitioners shall be entitled to the benefit of the proviso for purposes of import of mutton unless any amendment thereof.

Thereafter, the Government issued Notification, SRO 202 dated 19.07.2005 amending the 1973 Order whereby the words duly certified by the Union in condition no.1; condition no.7 and the word Union in condition no.8 added vide notification SRO 169 dated 16.06.2005 were deleted.

The writ petition,
OWP no.299/2005 was ultimately dismissed in default on 17.02.2012.
4. Meanwhile, the Government of India enacted Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short FSSA, 2006) which admittedly is applicable to the State of Jammu and Kashmir as well.

Section 1(2) of the Act says that it extends to the whole of India; whereas Section 1(3) says that it shall come Chinar Sheep And Goat Suppliers Welfare ... vs State Of J&K And Ors on 24 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129687876/
2 into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the official Gazette,
appoint.

sentences.text: The Act was published in the Gazette of India (Extraordinary) Part-II, Section 1, issue no.40 dated 24.08.2006.
Section 97 of the Act deals with the repeal and savings.

Sub-section (1) of Section 97 prescribes that with effect from such date as the Central Government may appoint in this behalf, the enactment and Orders specified in the Second Schedule shall stand repealed.
The Acts and Orders shown in the Second Schedule include the Meat Food Products Order, 1973 and any other order issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 relating to food.

5. After the promulgation of the FSSA 2006, the Health Officer, Srinagar Municipal Corporation, as being the Designated Officer under the Act, addressed communication dated 30.04.2012 to the Director, Consumer Affairs and Public Distribution, Srinagar, to the following effect:
This office is being approached by association of mutton dealers (both wholesales and retailers) regarding provisions of Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 and clarification thereof.
Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, has been implemented from 5th August 2011 in India including the State of Jammu & Kashmir.
As a consequence all the acts (under section 97) related to food mentioned in schedule II of FSSA 2006 have been repealed which includes, Meat and Meat Products Act 1973.
Any other order issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955) related to food are also repealed, and MMPO / Act 1973, has been brought under the ambit of FSSA 2006.
The food authority and the State food safety authority specified in section 30(1), 36(1) & 37(1) of this Act shall be responsible for the enforcement of the provisions of the act.
As per FSSA 2006 the state government has constituted a separate agency for implementation of FSSA 2006 in the State of Jammu & Kashmir, headed by Commissioner of Food Safety J&K.

Under the same Act and subsequent notifications issued by the Commissioner Food Safety J&K (order No.FSAJKI/98 of 2011 dated 08/08/2011) all the areas covered under the jurisdiction of Srinagar Municipal Corporation, Health Officer SMC has been notified as the Designated Officer under the Act.
Regarding other districts, separate designated officers have been notified.

The designated Officer will be the licensing / registration authority for their respective jurisdictions.
6.

The aforesaid communication has been challenged in OWP no.782/2012 on the ground that though Section 31 of FSSA 2006 provides for Licensing and Registration of Food Business, yet the said Section does not provide for possession of a licence for import of live sheep and goat and that the respondents are unauthorisedly and without any jurisdiction/competence seeking to enforce non-existent provisions of law against the petitioners for import of live stock from outside the State.
The petitioners also alleged interference and impediments caused to the petitioners in importing mutton in the shape of live stock.

In CMP no.1343/2012 accompanying the aforesaid writ petition,
the learned Writ Court vide order dated 15.06.2012 directed the respondents not to cause any Chinar Sheep And Goat Suppliers Welfare ... vs State Of J&K And Ors on 24 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129687876/
3 interference with the business of the petitioners for import of live stock (sheep and goat) from outside the State provided no handicap and no fetters or restrictions are applicable.
7.

sentences.text:
On 05.09.2013, the Director, Consumer Affairs and Public Distribution, Srinagar issued order no.
02-DCAPDK of 2013/Sup, professed to be issued in terms of Rule 10 of 1973 Order, whereby the Director issued certain directions for strict compliance by the wholesale Mutton Dealers of Kashmir Valley.

These included the directions that the Mutton Wholesalers should obtain license if not obtained so far from the Directorate of CAPD within the prescribed time fixed by it in order to carry out their wholesale business in Kashmir Valley; that for import of livestock the licensed wholesaler shall have to take a set of devised Proforma duly signed by the designated officer of the directorate;
and that it should be noted with caution that no livestock shall be allowed to be imported to valley by any person without having completed the necessary formalities required for the purpose.

It was provided that in case said import has not been found to be within the prescribed rules so devised,
the livestock carried in contravention of the rules was be put to auction on spot and the delinquent treated under the provisions of the relevant Act.
8. The aforesaid order dated 05.09.2013 has been challenged by the petitioners in other writ petition, OWP no.1277/2013.
When the matter came up for consideration before the Court, the learned Writ Court on 12.09.2013 ordered stay of the said order.

9. Subsequently, the petitioners filed yet another writ petition, OWP no.1434/2013 on the ground that during the pendency of writ petition, OWP no.1277/2013 and operation of the stay order, the respondents have seized various truck loads of livestock imported by the petitioners and other members of their association and put them to auction without any power or authority.

It is averred in the petition that the petitioners are wholesale license holders issued in their favour by respondent no.2 (Director, Consumer Affairs and Public Distribution) in terms of the provisions of SRO 646 for conducting wholesale business of mutton / livestock in the State and that, after expiry of the said licenses, they have applied for renewal thereof in terms of communication dated 09.04.2013, but the same have not been renewed by the respondent.
The respondents are however interfering with the business of the petitioners.

The writ petition has been filed with the prayer that the respondents may be commanded to renew the wholesale licenses of the petitioners for conducting wholesale business of mutton/livestock in Kashmir Division and that the respondents may further be commanded not to insist upon possession of license of any kind to be possessed by the petitioners for import of mutton/livestock from outside the State and not to confiscate, seize or put to auction such livestock imported by the petitioners.

It needs a mention here that when the writ petition came up for consideration before the Court, the learned Writ Court ordered its listing before this Court alongwith PIL no.01/2012.
10.

It may be mentioned here that petitioners also moved CMP no.2135/2013 stating therein that despite Court order dated 12.09.2013 staying operation of the order dated 05.09.2013, impugned in OWP no.1277/2013, truckloads of livestock being imported by the members of the petitioner association, namely, Mukhtar Ahmad, Abdul Salam Yachkoti, Nazir Ahmad, Abdul Rashid Kanoon and Abdul Rashid, loaded in trucks bearing registration nos. JK19/810, JK05C/8263, JK05A/4386,
JK 05C/6212 were seized at Lower Munda Check Post by Deputy Director, CAPD, Khanabal,
Chinar Sheep And Goat Suppliers Welfare ... vs State Of J&K And Ors on 24 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129687876/
4 Anantnag, under the instructions of respondent no.2, and that the said stocks were subsequently put to auction on 20.09.2013 by respondent no.2 through field functionaries / officials illegally and unauthorisedly.

sentences.text: It was further stated in the application that on 22.09.2013 three more truck loads of livestock loaded in trucks bearing registration nos. JK05B/4328, JK05B/2450 and JK01A/4003 have also been seized and put to auction.
In the application, it has been prayed that the respondents may be directed to release the auction money in their favour.

The petitioners, thereafter, moved another CMP, bearing CMP no. 2312/2013 stating therein that on 04.10.2013 the respondents seized truckload of livestock loaded in truck no.9778-PB07Q at Lower Munda.
The petitioners prayed that the respondents may be directed to release the livestock in their favour.
11. In their reply/objections filed in response to OWP no.1277/2013, the respondents have stated that respondent no.2 has put on hold the order dated 05.09.2013.

It is further, inter alia, stated that the petitioners do not possess valid licences for carrying on the business of mutton as required under Sub-clause (i) and (ii) of Clause 3 of the 1973 Order; that sub-clause (e) of Clause 15 of the 1973 Order was modified vide SRO 176 dated 29.06.2009 whereby the Licensing Authority or any officer duly authorised by him could seize and confiscate any stock of mutton in respect of which a contravention of the order has been, is being, or is about to be committed and, thereafter, put the same to auction and deposit the proceeds of the amount so recovered from the auction in the Government treasury.

It is admitted that the respondents, while exercising the above powers,
confiscated livestock belonging to the petitioners who were importing the same under their trade practice for their further sale in the Valley without any valid authority or licence, and that the respondents conducted auction of said stocks and deposited the sale proceeds in the Government treasury in accordance with the mandate of SRO 176 dated 29.06.2009.

Annexure R5 appended to the reply/objections at page 15 is a communication addressed by Assistant Director, CAPD,
Srinagar, addressed to the Treasury Officer requesting him to receive Rs.10,16,000.00 (Ten lac sixteen thousand only) on account of auction of illegal import of livestock (sheep) into the valley on 20.09.2013 and credit the same to account head 4408.

Similarly, annexure R5 at page 16 is another identical letter whereby Rs.3,12,000.00 have been deposited into the Government treasury in account head 4408-Food.
12.
It may be mentioned here that on 26.09.2013 while directing these matters to be listed for hearing, this Court directed that the auction amount be deposited with the Registrar Judicial of this Court.

It is reported by Mr. Tariq Ahmad Lone, learned counsel for the respondent no.2 that part of the auction money which has not so far been credited into the Government treasury is being deposited with the Registrar Judicial pursuant to the said order by order dated 26.09.2013 of this Court.

13. During the course of hearing, Mr. Tariq Ahmad Lone, learned counsel for the respondent no.2,
made a statement at the Bar that the respondents are ready to consider the pending applications of the petitioners for renewal of their licences.
His statement is taken on record.

Now that order dated 05.09.2013 has also been put on hold, the only question that remains to be determined is whether it was legally permissible for the respondents to seize and auction the livestock imported by the petitioners into the Valley.

sentences.text:
The submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners in this connection are two fold:
first, that after the promulgation of the FSSA 2006, the 1973 Order and all subsequent notifications passed pursuant thereto stand repealed; second, that even if it be assumed that respondents could still act under the 1973 Order, then in terms of Clause 3 thereof, petitioners are not required to have any licence for purposes of importing livestock (sheep and goat) into the State/Valley.

15. Learned counsel for the respondents, on the other hand, referred to and relied on SRO 176 dated 29.06.2009 to contend that the respondents are authorised to seize and confiscate mutton if there is contravention of the order or such a contravention is being or is about to be committed.
He submitted that since the livestock was being imported for sale, for which the petitioners did not possess valid licences, the respondents were within their powers to seize and confiscate the same.
16. We have already quoted Clause 3 of the 1973 Order in this judgment.

The restriction on carrying on the business of Mutton as Wholesaler, Broker or Retailer, except under and in accordance with a licence issued in that behalf by the Licensing Authority is imposed by Clause 3 of the 1973 Order.
The proviso added after sub-clause (1) thereof in terms of SRO 311 dated 13.06.1979 clearly states that nothing in this Clause shall apply to import of Mutton into the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

The language of the proviso makes it manifest that the restriction imposed by Clause 3(1) and the condition of having licence as envisaged therein for carrying on the business of Mutton does not apply to import of it into the State.

It is true that after the livestock is imported into the State /
Valley, the person importing the same has necessarily to have a licence to conduct its sale for which he needs to have a valid licence.

And going by the language used in SRO 176 of 29.06.2009, the respondents could seize and confiscate any stock in respect of which it is satisfied, inter alia, that a contravention of the 1973 order is about to be committed.

Once a person is found importing livestock, the competent authority can reasonably be satisfied that a contravention of the order is about to be committed because an importer of the livestock would not be importing it for anything other than the purpose of sale for which he needs to have a valid licence.
17. In the instant case, however, the stocks have been seized not because the competent authority or authorities were satisfied that a contravention was about to be committed.
They have instead seized and confiscated the stock of the petitioners on the ground that the stocks were being illegally imported.

This becomes clear from a bare reading of the communications addressed by Assistant Director, CAPD, Anantnag, to the District Treasury Officer, Anantnag, whereby the auction money of the livestock seized and confiscated from the petitioners has been deposited into the treasury.

The communication reads as under:
Kindly receive an amount of rupees 10,16,000/- (ten lac sixteen thousand only)
received during the auction of illegal import of live stocks (sheep) into the valley on 20.09.2013 a/n and credit the same to account head 408.
18.
It thus becomes manifest that the petitioners livestock was seized and confiscated terming its import as illegal.
It is reiterated here that in terms of Clause 3 of the 1973 Order, import of livestock without licence does not become illegal, its sale without a licence is illegal.

Had the Assistant Director in the aforesaid communications said that he was satisfied that a contravention of the order Chinar Sheep And Goat Suppliers Welfare ... vs State Of J&K And Ors on 24 October, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129687876/
6 was about to be committed in respect of such livestock, then the matter would have been different.

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, the seizure and confiscation of the petitioners imported livestock by the respondents and its subsequent auction by them is not authorised by the provision of Clause 3 of the 1973 Order.
20. All connected CMPs shall stand accordingly settled and disposed of.
21. Copy of order be placed on each file.

(Ali Mohammad Magrey) (M.M. Kumar)
